questions.question: NgModule vs Standalone components in Angular — what's the difference?
questions.title: NgModule vs Standalone Components (Angular 14+) — Migration Guide
questions.direct_answer:
NgModule vs Standalone components in Angular — what's the difference?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** NgModules wrap declarations/imports/providers; standalone components (v14+) eliminate boilerplate and are the new default.

**Classic weak answer:** Still starting new projects with AppModule in 2026 — Angular 17+ defaults to standalone and modules are considered legacy.

**Senior finish:** Note Angular 17+ CLI generates standalone by default and the roadmap deprecates NgModule for new code.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **NgModule vs Standalone Components (Angular 14+) — Migration Guide** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** NgModule vs Standalone components in Angular — what's the difference?

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **NgModules wrap declarations/imports/providers; standalone components (v14+) eliminate boilerplate and are the new default**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Still starting new projects with AppModule in 2026 — Angular 17+ defaults to standalone and modules are considered legacy**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Note Angular 17+ CLI generates standalone by default and the roadmap deprecates NgModule for new code**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** NgModules wrap declarations/imports/providers; standalone components (v14+) eliminate boilerplate and are the new default
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **still starting new projects with AppModule in 2026 — Angular 17+ defaults to standalone and modules are considered legacy** and what you do instead.

questions.question: What is the @Component decorator in Angular? Explain selector, template, and styles.
questions.title: @Component in Angular — selector, template, styles Explained
questions.direct_answer:
What is the @Component decorator in Angular? Explain selector, template, and styles.

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** @Component metadata: selector, template/templateUrl, styles/styleUrls, changeDetection, providers, standalone.

**Classic weak answer:** Using inline templates for complex UIs — prefer templateUrl and style files for separation of concerns.

**Senior finish:** Show OnPush change detection on the decorator and how to opt into standalone mode.
